item.title: National Security Cannot Be an Afterthought in Antitrust Enforcement
item.description: Antitrust remedies can reshape U.S. tech leadership relative to China. National security experts should assess those consequences before the government commits to enforcement, not after.

item.title: Lebanon’s Imperiled Transition: The Need for an Urgent Reset
item.description: As Lebanon approaches the two-year mark of the new leadership’s mandate, progress toward real sovereignty and fundamental reform appears dangerously stalled. An urgent strategic reboot is necessary.

item.title: Post-Election Thoughts
item.description: In this special edition of his weekly column, Bill Reinsch unpacks the results of the 2026 midterm elections and discusses how the Democratic majorities in the House and the Senate might approach trade policy in the next Congress.

item.title: Preparing for the Next Crisis
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East highlights the importance of early warning systems, emergency communications, and community-based warning mechanisms amid recurrent surges of conflict in the region.

item.title: What’s in Canada’s New National Security Plan?
item.description: CSIS experts unpack Canada’s first national security strategy in more than 20 years, including its timing, priorities, implications for continental defense, and possible reactions from the United States.

item.title: States Weekly: November 4, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers November 4, 2026.

item.title: The Future of USMCA
item.description: In this week’s column, William Alan Reinsch discusses the difference between the type of North American trade agreement that the United States wants and the type of agreement that would benefit all three countries on the continent.

item.title: Deepfakes Are Dominating Global Elections, and Regulation Is Playing Catch-Up
item.description: As AI-generated deepfakes become increasingly prevalent in elections worldwide, governments are struggling to distinguish political expression from deception and enforce regulations before misleading content reaches voters.
